title: Rabanal star apple: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Rabanal star apple: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Rabanal star apple is a star apple variety from Sixto R. Pascua, Jr. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Rabanal is a registered star apple variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Ca 02. Sixto R. Pascua, Jr bred it. Its record notes a yield of 1,000 fruits.

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [star apple variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Rabanal star apple
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Rabanal was about 53 years old and about 20 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 1,000 fruits. It bears regularly, with fruit in March May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit star apple fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Rabanal weighs about 379.7 grams, and its shape is globose. The flesh is creamy white to purple and smooth and fine. Its sweetness measured 18.9 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 69.6 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as March May, bearing regular.
Where and when to plant Rabanal star apple

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: The record shows a recorded yield of 1,000 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Rabanal?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
